If the `to` parameter is a phone number, `From` must also be a phone number. |

If no `status_callback_event` is specified, we will send the `completed` status. If an `application_sid` parameter is present, this parameter is ignored. URLs must contain a valid hostname (underscores are not permitted). |
| <code>statusCallbackEvent?</code> | <code>string[]</code> | The call progress events that we will send to the `status_callback` URL. Can be: `initiated`, `ringing`, `answered`, and `completed`. If no event is specified, we send the `completed` status. If you want to receive multiple events, specify each one in a separate `status_callback_event` parameter. See the code sample for [monitoring call progress](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/api/call-resource?code-sample=code-create-a-call-resource-and-specify-a-statuscallbackevent&code-sdk-version=json). If an `application_sid` is present, this parameter is ignored. |
| <code>statusCallbackMethod?</code> | <code>[StatusCallbackMethod8](src/models/status-callback-method8.ts)</code> | The HTTP method we should use when calling the `status_callback` URL. Can be: `GET` or `POST` and the default is `POST`. If an `application_sid` parameter is present, this parameter is ignored. |
| <code>sendDigits?</code> | <code>string</code> | The string of keys to dial after connecting to the number, with a maximum length of 32 digits. Valid digits in the string include any digit (`0`-`9`), '`A`', '`B`', '`C`', '`D`', '`#`', and '`*`'. You can also use '`w`' to insert a half-second pause and '`W`' to insert a one-second pause. For example, to pause for one second after connecting and then dial extension 1234 followed by the # key, set this parameter to `W1234#`. Be sure to URL-encode this string because the '`#`' character has special meaning in a URL. If both `SendDigits` and `MachineDetection` parameters are provided, then `MachineDetection` will be ignored. |
| <code>timeout?</code> | <code>number</code> | The integer number of seconds that we should allow the phone to ring before assuming there is no answer. The default is `60` seconds and the maximum is `600` seconds. For some call flows, we will add a 5-second buffer to the timeout value you provide. For this reason, a timeout value of 10 seconds could result in an actual timeout closer to 15 seconds. You can set this to a short time, such as `15` seconds, to hang up before reaching an answering machine or voicemail. |
| <code>record?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether to record the call. Can be `true` to record the phone call, or `false` to not. The default is `false`. The `recording_url` is sent to the `status_callback` URL. |
| <code>recordingChannels?</code> | <code>string</code> | The number of channels in the final recording. Can be: `mono` or `dual`. The default is `mono`. `mono` records both legs of the call in a single channel of the recording file. `dual` records each leg to a separate channel of the recording file. The first channel of a dual-channel recording contains the parent call and the second channel contains the child call. |
| <code>recordingStatusCallback?</code> | <code>string</code> | The URL that we call when the recording is available to be accessed. |
| <code>recordingStatusCallbackMethod?</code> | <code>[RecordingStatusCallbackMethod](src/models/recording-status-callback-method.ts)</code> | The HTTP method we should use when calling the `recording_status_callback` URL. Can be: `GET` or `POST` and the default is `POST`. |
| <code>recordingConfigurationId?</code> | <code>string</code> | The identifier of the configuration to be used when creating and processing the recording |
| <code>sipAuthUsername?</code> | <code>string</code> | The username used to authenticate the caller making a SIP call. |
| <code>sipAuthPassword?</code> | <code>string</code> | The password required to authenticate the user account specified in `sip_auth_username`. |
| <code>machineDetection?</code> | <code>string</code> | Whether to detect if a human, answering machine, or fax has picked up the call. Can be: `Enable` or `DetectMessageEnd`. Use `Enable` if you would like us to return `AnsweredBy` as soon as the called party is identified. Use `DetectMessageEnd`, if you would like to leave a message on an answering machine. If `send_digits` is provided, this parameter is ignored. For more information, see [Answering Machine Detection](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/answering-machine-detection). |
| <code>machineDetectionTimeout?</code> | <code>number</code> | The number of seconds that we should attempt to detect an answering machine before timing out and sending a voice request with `AnsweredBy` of `unknown`. The default timeout is 30 seconds. |
| <code>recordingStatusCallbackEvent?</code> | <code>string[]</code> | The recording status events that will trigger calls to the URL specified in `recording_status_callback`. Can be: `in-progress`, `completed` and `absent`. Defaults to `completed`. Separate  multiple values with a space. |
| <code>trim?</code> | <code>string</code> | Whether to trim any leading and trailing silence from the recording. Can be: `trim-silence` or `do-not-trim` and the default is `trim-silence`. |
| <code>callerId?</code> | <code>string</code> | The phone number, SIP address, or Client identifier that made this call. Phone numbers are in [E.164 format](https://wwnw.twilio.com/docs/glossary/what-e164) (e.g., +16175551212). SIP addresses are formatted as `name@company.com`. |
| <code>machineDetectionSpeechThreshold?</code> | <code>number</code> | The number of milliseconds that is used as the measuring stick for the length of the speech activity, where durations lower than this value will be interpreted as a human and longer than this value as a machine. Possible Values: 1000-6000. Default: 2400. |
| <code>machineDetectionSpeechEndThreshold?</code> | <code>number</code> | The number of milliseconds of silence after speech activity at which point the speech activity is considered complete. Possible Values: 500-5000. Default: 1200. |
| <code>machineDetectionSilenceTimeout?</code> | <code>number</code> | The number of milliseconds of initial silence after which an `unknown` AnsweredBy result will be returned. Possible Values: 2000-10000. Default: 5000. |
| <code>asyncAmd?</code> | <code>string</code> | Select whether to perform answering machine detection in the background. Default, blocks the execution of the call until Answering Machine Detection is completed. Can be: `true` or `false`. |
| <code>asyncAmdStatusCallback?</code> | <code>string</code> | The URL that we should call using the `async_amd_status_callback_method` to notify customer application whether the call was answered by human, machine or fax. |
| <code>asyncAmdStatusCallbackMethod?</code> | <code>[AsyncAmdStatusCallbackMethod](src/models/async-amd-status-callback-method.ts)</code> | The HTTP method we should use when calling the `async_amd_status_callback` URL. Can be: `GET` or `POST` and the default is `POST`. |
| <code>byoc?</code> | <code>string</code> | The SID of a BYOC (Bring Your Own Carrier) trunk to route this call with. Note that `byoc` is only meaningful when `to` is a phone number; it will otherwise be ignored. (Beta) |
| <code>callReason?</code> | <code>string</code> | The Reason for the outgoing call. Use it to specify the purpose of the call that is presented on the called party's phone. (Branded Calls Beta) |
| <code>callToken?</code> | <code>string</code> | A token string needed to invoke a forwarded call. A call_token is generated when an incoming call is received on a Twilio number. Pass an incoming call's call_token value to a forwarded call via the call_token parameter when creating a new call. A forwarded call should bear the same CallerID of the original incoming call. |
| <code>recordingTrack?</code> | <code>string</code> | The audio track to record for the call. Can be: `inbound`, `outbound` or `both`. The default is `both`. `inbound` records the audio that is received by Twilio. `outbound` records the audio that is generated from Twilio. `both` records the audio that is received and generated by Twilio. |


### Parameters

<dd>

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code>accountSid</code> | <code>string</code> | The SID of the [Account](https://www.twilio.com/docs/iam/api/account) that is associated with the Media resources. |
| <code>messageSid</code> | <code>string</code> | The SID of the Message resource that is associated with the Media resources. |
| <code>dateCreated?</code> | <code>Date</code> (date-time) | Only include Media resources that were created on this date. Specify a date as `YYYY-MM-DD` in GMT, for example: `2009-07-06`, to read Media that were created on this date. You can also specify an inequality, such as `StartTime<=YYYY-MM-DD`, to read Media that were created on or before midnight of this date, and `StartTime>=YYYY-MM-DD` to read Media that were created on or after midnight of this date. |
| <code>dateCreatedQuery?</code> | <code>Date</code> (date-time) | Only include Media resources that were created on this date. Specify a date as `YYYY-MM-DD` in GMT, for example: `2009-07-06`, to read Media that were created on this date. You can also specify an inequality, such as `StartTime<=YYYY-MM-DD`, to read Media that were created on or before midnight of this date, and `StartTime>=YYYY-MM-DD` to read Media that were created on or after midnight of this date. |
| <code>dateCreatedQueryQuery?</code> | <code>Date</code> (date-time) | Only include Media resources that were created on this date. Specify a date as `YYYY-MM-DD` in GMT, for example: `2009-07-06`, to read Media that were created on this date. You can also specify an inequality, such as `StartTime<=YYYY-MM-DD`, to read Media that were created on or before midnight of this date, and `StartTime>=YYYY-MM-DD` to read Media that were created on or after midnight of this date. |
| <code>pageSize?</code> | <code>number</code> | How many resources to return in each list page. The default is 50, and the maximum is 1000. |
| <code>page?</code> | <code>number</code> | The page index. This value is simply for client state. |
| <code>pageToken?</code> | <code>string</code> | The page token. This is provided by the API. |

A `validity_period` greater than `5` is recommended. [Learn more about the validity period](https://www.twilio.com/blog/take-more-control-of-outbound-messages-using-validity-period-html) |

| <code>sendAt?</code> | <code>Date</code> (date-time) | The time that Twilio will send the message. Must be in ISO 8601 format. |

If values are not defined in the `content_variables` parameter, the [Template's default placeholder values](https://www.twilio.com/docs/content/content-api-resources#create-templates) are used. |
| <code>riskCheck?</code> | <code>[MessageEnumRiskCheck](src/models/message-enum-risk-check.ts)</code> | Include this parameter with a value of `disable` to skip any kind of risk check on the respective message request. |
| <code>from?</code> | <code>string</code> | The sender's Twilio phone number (in [E.164](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.164) format), [alphanumeric sender ID](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sms/quickstart), [Wireless SIM](https://www.twilio.com/docs/iot/wireless/programmable-wireless-send-machine-machine-sms-commands), [short code](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/messaging/channels/sms/short-codes), or [channel address](https://www.twilio.com/docs/messaging/channels) (e.g., `whatsapp:+15554449999`). The value of the `from` parameter must be a sender that is hosted within Twilio and belongs to the Account creating the Message. If you are using `messaging_service_sid`, this parameter can be empty (Twilio assigns a `from` value from the Messaging Service's Sender Pool) or you can provide a specific sender from your Sender Pool. |
| <code>fallbackFrom?</code> | <code>string</code> | A fallback SMS sender to use when the recipient cannot be reached over RCS. This parameter may only be used when also providing a [Messaging Service](https://twilio.com/docs/messaging/services) containing an RCS sender. The fallback SMS sender must be either a Twilio phone number (in [E.164](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.164) format), [alphanumeric sender ID](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sms/quickstart), or [short code](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/messaging/channels/sms/short-codes), hosted within Twilio and belong to the Account creating the Message. |
| <code>messagingServiceSid?</code> | <code>string</code> | The SID of the [Messaging Service](https://www.twilio.com/docs/messaging/services) you want to associate with the Message. When this parameter is provided and the `from` parameter is omitted, Twilio selects the optimal sender from the Messaging Service's Sender Pool. You may also provide a `from` parameter if you want to use a specific Sender from the Sender Pool. |
| <code>body2?</code> | <code>string</code> | The text content of the outgoing message. Can be up to 1,600 characters in length. SMS only: If the `body` contains more than 160 [GSM-7](https://www.twilio.com/docs/glossary/what-is-gsm-7-character-encoding) characters (or 70 [UCS-2](https://www.twilio.com/docs/glossary/what-is-ucs-2-character-encoding) characters), the message is segmented and charged accordingly. For long `body` text, consider using the [send_as_mms parameter](https://www.twilio.com/blog/mms-for-long-text-messages). |
| <code>mediaUrl?</code> | <code>string[]</code> | The URL of media to include in the Message content. `jpeg`, `jpg`, `gif`, and `png` file types are fully supported by Twilio and content is formatted for delivery on destination devices. The media size limit is 5 MB for supported file types (`jpeg`, `jpg`, `png`, `gif`) and 500 KB for [other types](https://www.twilio.com/docs/messaging/guides/accepted-mime-types) of accepted media. To send more than one image in the message, provide multiple `media_url` parameters in the POST request. You can include up to ten `media_url` parameters per message. [International](https://support.twilio.com/hc/en-us/articles/223179808-Sending-and-receiving-MMS-messages) and [carrier](https://support.twilio.com/hc/en-us/articles/223133707-Is-MMS-supported-for-all-carriers-in-US-and-Canada-) limits apply. |
| <code>contentSid?</code> | <code>string</code> | For [Content Editor/API](https://www.twilio.com/docs/content) only: The SID of the Content Template to be used with the Message, e.g., `HXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX`. If this parameter is not provided, a Content Template is not used. Find the SID in the Console on the Content Editor page. For Content API users, the SID is found in Twilio's response when [creating the Template](https://www.twilio.com/docs/content/content-api-resources#create-templates) or by [fetching your Templates](https://www.twilio.com/docs/content/content-api-resources#fetch-all-content-resources). |

Phone numbers are in [E.164](https://www.twilio.com/docs/glossary/what-e164) format (e.g., +16175551212). Client identifiers are formatted `client:name`. If using a phone number, it must be a Twilio number or a Verified [outgoing caller id](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/api/outgoing-caller-ids) for your account. Phone numbers are in [E.164](https://www.twilio.com/docs/glossary/what-e164) format (e.g., +16175551212). SIP addresses are formatted as `sip:name@company.com`. Client identifiers are formatted `client:name`. TwiML App identifiers are formatted `app:<APP_SID>`. The default value is `60`. We always add a 5-second timeout buffer to outgoing calls, so  value of 10 would result in an actual timeout that was closer to 15 seconds. |

Can be: `true` or `false` and the default is `true`. If `false` and the conference has not started, the participant is muted and hears background music until another participant starts the conference. |
| <code>endConferenceOnExit?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether to end the conference when the participant leaves. Can be: `true` or `false` and defaults to `false`. |

The default value is the URL of our standard hold music. If you do not want anything to play while waiting for the conference to start, specify an empty string by setting `wait_url` to `''`. For more details on the allowable verbs within the `waitUrl`, see the `waitUrl` attribute in the [<Conference> TwiML instruction](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/twiml/conference#attributes-waiturl). |
| <code>waitMethod?</code> | <code>[WaitMethod](src/models/wait-method.ts)</code> | The HTTP method we should use to call `wait_url`. Can be `GET` or `POST` and the default is `POST`. When using a static audio file, this should be `GET` so that we can cache the file. |
| <code>earlyMedia?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether to allow an agent to hear the state of the outbound call, including ringing or disconnect messages. Can be: `true` or `false` and defaults to `true`. |
| <code>maxParticipants?</code> | <code>number</code> | The maximum number of participants in the conference. Can be a positive integer from `2` to `250`. The default value is `250`. |
| <code>conferenceRecord?</code> | <code>string</code> | Whether to record the conference the participant is joining. Can be: `true`, `false`, `record-from-start`, and `do-not-record`. The default value is `false`. |
| <code>conferenceTrim?</code> | <code>string</code> | Whether to trim leading and trailing silence from the conference recording. Can be: `trim-silence` or `do-not-trim` and defaults to `trim-silence`. |
| <code>conferenceStatusCallback?</code> | <code>string</code> | The URL we should call using the `conference_status_callback_method` when the conference events in `conference_status_callback_event` occur. Only the value set by the first participant to join the conference is used. Subsequent `conference_status_callback` values are ignored. |

| <code>recordingStatusCallbackMethod?</code> | <code>[RecordingStatusCallbackMethod2](src/models/recording-status-callback-method2.ts)</code> | The HTTP method we should use when we call `recording_status_callback`. Can be: `GET` or `POST` and defaults to `POST`. |

Can be:`us1`, `us2`, `ie1`, `de1`, `sg1`, `br1`, `au1`, or `jp1`. |
| <code>conferenceRecordingStatusCallback?</code> | <code>string</code> | The URL we should call using the `conference_recording_status_callback_method` when the conference recording is available. |
| <code>conferenceRecordingStatusCallbackMethod?</code> | <code>[ConferenceRecordingStatusCallbackMethod](src/models/conference-recording-status-callback-method.ts)</code> | The HTTP method we should use to call `conference_recording_status_callback`. Can be: `GET` or `POST` and defaults to `POST`. |
| <code>recordingStatusCallbackEvent?</code> | <code>string[]</code> | The recording state changes that should generate a call to `recording_status_callback`. Can be: `started`, `in-progress`, `paused`, `resumed`, `stopped`, `completed`, `failed`, and `absent`. Separate multiple values with a space, ex: `'in-progress completed failed'`. |
| <code>conferenceRecordingStatusCallbackEvent?</code> | <code>string[]</code> | The conference recording state changes that generate a call to `conference_recording_status_callback`. Can be: `in-progress`, `completed`, `failed`, and `absent`. Separate multiple values with a space, ex: `'in-progress completed failed'` |
| <code>coaching?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether the participant is coaching another call. Can be: `true` or `false`. If not present, defaults to `false` unless `call_sid_to_coach` is defined. If `true`, `call_sid_to_coach` must be defined. |
| <code>callSidToCoach?</code> | <code>string</code> | The SID of the participant who is being `coached`. The participant being coached is the only participant who can hear the participant who is `coaching`. |
| <code>jitterBufferSize?</code> | <code>string</code> | Jitter buffer size for the connecting participant. Twilio will use this setting to apply Jitter Buffer before participant's audio is mixed into the conference. Can be: `off`, `small`, `medium`, and `large`. Default to `large`. |
| <code>byoc?</code> | <code>string</code> | The SID of a BYOC (Bring Your Own Carrier) trunk to route this call with. Note that `byoc` is only meaningful when `to` is a phone number; it will otherwise be ignored. (Beta) |
| <code>callerId?</code> | <code>string</code> | The phone number, Client identifier, or username portion of SIP address that made this call. Phone numbers are in [E.164](https://www.twilio.com/docs/glossary/what-e164) format (e.g., +16175551212). Client identifiers are formatted `client:name`. If using a phone number, it must be a Twilio number or a Verified [outgoing caller id](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/api/outgoing-caller-ids) for your account. If the `to` parameter is a phone number, `callerId` must also be a phone number. If `to` is sip address, this value of `callerId` should be a username portion to be used to populate the From header that is passed to the SIP endpoint. |
| <code>callReason?</code> | <code>string</code> | The Reason for the outgoing call. Use it to specify the purpose of the call that is presented on the called party's phone. (Branded Calls Beta) |
| <code>recordingTrack?</code> | <code>string</code> | The audio track to record for the call. Can be: `inbound`, `outbound` or `both`. The default is `both`. `inbound` records the audio that is received by Twilio. `outbound` records the audio that is sent from Twilio. `both` records the audio that is received and sent by Twilio. |
| <code>recordingConfigurationId?</code> | <code>string</code> | The identifier of the configuration to be used when creating and processing the recording |
| <code>timeLimit?</code> | <code>number</code> | The maximum duration of the call in seconds. Constraints depend on account and configuration. |
| <code>machineDetection?</code> | <code>string</code> | Whether to detect if a human, answering machine, or fax has picked up the call. Can be: `Enable` or `DetectMessageEnd`. Use `Enable` if you would like us to return `AnsweredBy` as soon as the called party is identified. Use `DetectMessageEnd`, if you would like to leave a message on an answering machine. For more information, see [Answering Machine Detection](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/answering-machine-detection). |
| <code>machineDetectionTimeout?</code> | <code>number</code> | The number of seconds that we should attempt to detect an answering machine before timing out and sending a voice request with `AnsweredBy` of `unknown`. The default timeout is 30 seconds. |
| <code>machineDetectionSpeechThreshold?</code> | <code>number</code> | The number of milliseconds that is used as the measuring stick for the length of the speech activity, where durations lower than this value will be interpreted as a human and longer than this value as a machine. Possible Values: 1000-6000. Default: 2400. |
| <code>machineDetectionSpeechEndThreshold?</code> | <code>number</code> | The number of milliseconds of silence after speech activity at which point the speech activity is considered complete. Possible Values: 500-5000. Default: 1200. |
| <code>machineDetectionSilenceTimeout?</code> | <code>number</code> | The number of milliseconds of initial silence after which an `unknown` AnsweredBy result will be returned. Possible Values: 2000-10000. Default: 5000. |
| <code>amdStatusCallback?</code> | <code>string</code> | The URL that we should call using the `amd_status_callback_method` to notify customer application whether the call was answered by human, machine or fax. |
| <code>amdStatusCallbackMethod?</code> | <code>[AmdStatusCallbackMethod](src/models/amd-status-callback-method.ts)</code> | The HTTP method we should use when calling the `amd_status_callback` URL. Can be: `GET` or `POST` and the default is `POST`. |
| <code>trim?</code> | <code>string</code> | Whether to trim any leading and trailing silence from the participant recording. Can be: `trim-silence` or `do-not-trim` and the default is `trim-silence`. |
| <code>callToken?</code> | <code>string</code> | A token string needed to invoke a forwarded call. A call_token is generated when an incoming call is received on a Twilio number. | <code>clientNotificationUrl?</code> | <code>string</code> | The URL that we should use to deliver `push call notification`. |

| <code>callSid</code> | <code>string</code> | The [Call](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/api/call-resource) SID or label of the participant to update. Non URL safe characters in a label must be percent encoded, for example, a space character is represented as %20. |
| <code>muted?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether the participant should be muted. Can be `true` or `false`. `true` will mute the participant, and `false` will un-mute them. Anything value other than `true` or `false` is interpreted as `false`. |
| <code>hold?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether the participant should be on hold. Can be: `true` or `false`. `true` puts the participant on hold, and `false` lets them rejoin the conference. |
| <code>holdUrl?</code> | <code>string</code> | The URL we call using the `hold_method` for music that plays when the participant is on hold. The URL may return an MP3 file, a WAV file, or a TwiML document that contains `<Play>`, `<Say>`, `<Pause>`, or `<Redirect>` verbs. |
| <code>holdMethod?</code> | <code>[HoldMethod](src/models/hold-method.ts)</code> | The HTTP method we should use to call `hold_url`. Can be: `GET` or `POST` and the default is `GET`. |
| <code>announceUrl?</code> | <code>string</code> | The URL we call using the `announce_method` for an announcement to the participant. The URL may return an MP3 file, a WAV file, or a TwiML document that contains `<Play>`, `<Say>`, `<Pause>`, or `<Redirect>` verbs. |
| <code>announceMethod?</code> | <code>[AnnounceMethod1](src/models/announce-method1.ts)</code> | The HTTP method we should use to call `announce_url`. Can be: `GET` or `POST` and defaults to `POST`. |
| <code>waitUrl?</code> | <code>string</code> | The URL that Twilio calls using the `wait_method` before the conference has started. The URL may return an MP3 file, a WAV file, or a TwiML document. The default value is the URL of our standard hold music. If you do not want anything to play while waiting for the conference to start, specify an empty string by setting `wait_url` to `''`. For more details on the allowable verbs within the `waitUrl`, see the `waitUrl` attribute in the [<Conference> TwiML instruction](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/twiml/conference#attributes-waiturl). |
| <code>waitMethod?</code> | <code>[WaitMethod](src/models/wait-method.ts)</code> | The HTTP method we should use to call `wait_url`. Can be `GET` or `POST` and the default is `POST`. When using a static audio file, this should be `GET` so that we can cache the file. |
| <code>beepOnExit?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether to play a notification beep to the conference when the participant exits. Can be: `true` or `false`. |
| <code>endConferenceOnExit?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether to end the conference when the participant leaves. Can be: `true` or `false` and defaults to `false`. |
| <code>coaching?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether the participant is coaching another call. Can be: `true` or `false`. If not present, defaults to `false` unless `call_sid_to_coach` is defined. If `true`, `call_sid_to_coach` must be defined. |
| <code>callSidToCoach?</code> | <code>string</code> | The SID of the participant who is being `coached`. The participant being coached is the only participant who can hear the participant who is `coaching`. |

</dd>
</dl>

| <code>callSid</code> | <code>string</code> | The SID of the call that will create the resource. Call leg associated with this sid is expected to provide payment information thru DTMF. |
| <code>idempotencyKey</code> | <code>string</code> | A unique token that will be used to ensure that multiple API calls with the same information do not result in multiple transactions. This should be a unique string value per API call and can be a randomly generated. |
| <code>statusCallback</code> | <code>string</code> | Provide an absolute or relative URL to receive status updates regarding your Pay session. Read more about the [expected StatusCallback values](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/api/payment-resource#statuscallback) |
| <code>bankAccountType?</code> | <code>[PaymentsEnumBankAccountType](src/models/payments-enum-bank-account-type.ts)</code> | Type of bank account if payment source is ACH. One of `consumer-checking`, `consumer-savings`, or `commercial-checking`. The default value is `consumer-checking`. |
| <code>chargeAmount?</code> | <code>number</code> | A positive decimal value less than 1,000,000 to charge against the credit card or bank account. Default currency can be overwritten with `currency` field. Leave blank or set to 0 to tokenize. |
| <code>currency?</code> | <code>string</code> | The currency of the `charge_amount`, formatted as [ISO 4127](http://www.iso.org/iso/home/standards/currency_codes.htm) format. The default value is `USD` and all values allowed from the Pay Connector are accepted. |
| <code>description?</code> | <code>string</code> | The description can be used to provide more details regarding the transaction. This information is submitted along with the payment details to the Payment Connector which are then posted on the transactions. |
| <code>input?</code> | <code>string</code> | A list of inputs that should be accepted. Currently only `dtmf` is supported. All digits captured during a pay session are redacted from the logs. |
| <code>minPostalCodeLength?</code> | <code>number</code> | A positive integer that is used to validate the length of the `PostalCode` inputted by the user. User must enter this many digits. |
| <code>parameter?</code> | <code>Record&lt;string, unknown&gt;</code> | A single-level JSON object used to pass custom parameters to payment processors. (Required for ACH payments). The information that has to be included here depends on the <Pay> Connector. [Read more](https://www.twilio.com/console/voice/pay-connectors). |
| <code>paymentConnector?</code> | <code>string</code> | This is the unique name corresponding to the Pay Connector installed in the Twilio Add-ons. Learn more about [<Pay> Connectors](https://www.twilio.com/console/voice/pay-connectors). The default value is `Default`. |
| <code>paymentMethod?</code> | <code>[PaymentsEnumPaymentMethod](src/models/payments-enum-payment-method.ts)</code> | Type of payment being captured. One of `credit-card` or `ach-debit`. The default value is `credit-card`. |
| <code>postalCode?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Indicates whether the credit card postal code (zip code) is a required piece of payment information that must be provided by the caller. The default is `true`. |
| <code>securityCode?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Indicates whether the credit card security code is a required piece of payment information that must be provided by the caller. The default is `true`. |
| <code>timeout?</code> | <code>number</code> | The number of seconds that <Pay> should wait for the caller to press a digit between each subsequent digit, after the first one, before moving on to validate the digits captured. The default is `5`, maximum is `600`. |
| <code>tokenType?</code> | <code>[PaymentsEnumTokenType](src/models/payments-enum-token-type.ts)</code> | Indicates whether the payment method should be tokenized as a `one-time`, `reusable`, or `payment-method` token. The default value is `reusable`. Do not enter a charge amount when tokenizing. If a charge amount is entered, the payment method will be charged and not tokenized. |
| <code>validCardTypes?</code> | <code>string</code> | Credit card types separated by space that Pay should accept. The default value is `visa mastercard amex` |
| <code>requireMatchingInputs?</code> | <code>string</code> | A comma-separated list of payment information fields that require the caller to enter the same value twice for confirmation. Supported values are `payment-card-number`, `expiration-date`, `security-code`, and `postal-code`. |
| <code>confirmation?</code> | <code>[Confirmation](src/models/confirmation.ts)</code> | Whether to prompt the caller to confirm their payment information before submitting to the payment gateway. If `true`, the caller will hear the last 4 digits of their card or account number and must press 1 to confirm or 2 to cancel. Default is `false`. |

To match wildcards at the beginning or end of the pattern, use `*` to match any single character or `%` to match a sequence of characters. If you use the wildcard patterns, it must include at least two non-meta-characters, and wildcards cannot be used between non-meta-characters. | <code>alphaSender</code> | <code>string</code> | The Alphanumeric Sender ID string. Can be up to 11 characters long. Valid characters are A-Z, a-z, 0-9, space, hyphen `-`, plus `+`, underscore `_` and ampersand `&`. This value cannot contain only numbers. |
| <code>isoCountryCode?</code> | <code>string</code> | The Optional Two Character ISO Country Code the Alphanumeric Sender ID will be used for. If the IsoCountryCode is not provided, a default Alpha Sender will be created that can be used across all countries. |

The opt-in response should include the Brand name, confirmation of opt-in enrollment to a recurring message campaign, how to get help, and clear description of how to opt-out. This field is required if end users can text in a keyword to start receiving messages from this campaign. 20 character minimum. 320 character maximum. |
| <code>optOutMessage?</code> | <code>string</code> | Upon receiving the opt-out keywords from the end users, Twilio customers are expected to send back an auto-generated response, which must provide acknowledgment of the opt-out request and confirmation that no further messages will be sent. It is also recommended that these opt-out messages include the brand name. This field is required if managing opt out keywords yourself (i.e. not using Twilio's Default or Advanced Opt Out features). 20 character minimum. 320 character maximum. |
| <code>helpMessage?</code> | <code>string</code> | When customers receive the help keywords from their end users, Twilio customers are expected to send back an auto-generated response; this may include the brand name and additional support contact information. This field is required if managing help keywords yourself (i.e. not using Twilio's Default or Advanced Opt Out features). 20 character minimum. 320 character maximum. |
| <code>optInKeywords?</code> | <code>string[]</code> | If end users can text in a keyword to start receiving messages from this campaign, those keywords must be provided. This field is required if end users can text in a keyword to start receiving messages from this campaign. Values must be alphanumeric. 255 character maximum. |
| <code>optOutKeywords?</code> | <code>string[]</code> | End users should be able to text in a keyword to stop receiving messages from this campaign. Those keywords must be provided. This field is required if managing opt out keywords yourself (i.e. not using Twilio's Default or Advanced Opt Out features). Values must be alphanumeric. 255 character maximum. |
| <code>helpKeywords?</code> | <code>string[]</code> | End users should be able to text in a keyword to receive help. Those keywords must be provided as part of the campaign registration request. This field is required if managing help keywords yourself (i.e. not using Twilio's Default or Advanced Opt Out features). Values must be alphanumeric. 255 character maximum. |
| <code>subscriberOptIn?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | A boolean that specifies whether campaign has Subscriber Optin or not. |
| <code>ageGated?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | A boolean that specifies whether campaign is age gated or not. |
| <code>directLending?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | A boolean that specifies whether campaign allows direct lending or not. |
| <code>privacyPolicyUrl?</code> | <code>string</code> | The URL of the privacy policy for the campaign. |
| <code>termsAndConditionsUrl?</code> | <code>string</code> | The URL of the terms and conditions for the campaign. |

This identifier should be immutable, not PII, length between 8 and 64 characters, and generated by your external system, such as your user's UUID, GUID, or SID. It can only contain dash (-) separated alphanumeric characters. |
| <code>factorSid</code> | <code>string</code> | The unique SID identifier of the Factor. |
| <code>expirationDate?</code> | <code>Date</code> (date-time) | The date-time when this Challenge expires, given in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format. The default value is five (5) minutes after Challenge creation. The max value is sixty (60) minutes after creation. |
| <code>detailsMessage?</code> | <code>string</code> | Shown to the user when the push notification arrives. Required when `factor_type` is `push`. Can be up to 256 characters in length |
| <code>detailsFields?</code> | <code>Record&lt;string, unknown&gt;[]</code> | A list of objects that describe the Fields included in the Challenge. Each object contains the label and value of the field, the label can be up to 36 characters in length and the value can be up to 128 characters in length. Used when `factor_type` is `push`. There can be up to 20 details fields. |
| <code>hiddenDetails?</code> | <code>Record&lt;string, unknown&gt;</code> | Details provided to give context about the Challenge. Not shown to the end user. It must be a stringified JSON with only strings values eg. `{"ip": "172.168.1.234"}`. Can be up to 1024 characters in length |
| <code>authPayload?</code> | <code>string</code> | Optional payload used to verify the Challenge upon creation. Only used with a Factor of type `totp` to carry the TOTP code that needs to be verified. For `TOTP` this value must be between 3 and 8 characters long. |

</dd>
</dl>

```ts
}
```

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code>serviceSid</code> | <code>string</code> | The unique SID identifier of the Service. |
| <code>identity</code> | <code>string</code> | Customer unique identity for the Entity owner of the Factor. This identifier should be immutable, not PII, length between 8 and 64 characters, and generated by your external system, such as your user's UUID, GUID, or SID. It can only contain dash (-) separated alphanumeric characters. |
| <code>sid</code> | <code>string</code> | A 34 character string that uniquely identifies this Factor. |
| <code>authPayload?</code> | <code>string</code> | The optional payload needed to verify the Factor for the first time. E.g. for a TOTP, the numeric code. |

| <code>configSdkVersion?</code> | <code>string</code> | The Verify Push SDK version used to configure the factor |
| <code>configTimeStep?</code> | <code>number</code> | Defines how often, in seconds, are TOTP codes generated. i.e, a new TOTP code is generated every time_step seconds. Must be between 20 and 60 seconds, inclusive |
| <code>configSkew?</code> | <code>number</code> | The number of time-steps, past and future, that are valid for validation of TOTP codes. Must be between 0 and 2, inclusive |
| <code>configCodeLength?</code> | <code>number</code> | Number of digits for generated TOTP codes. Must be between 3 and 8, inclusive |
| <code>configAlg?</code> | <code>[FactorEnumTotpAlgorithms](src/models/factor-enum-totp-algorithms.ts)</code> | - |
| <code>configNotificationPlatform?</code> | <code>string</code> | The transport technology used to generate the Notification Token. Can be `apn`, `fcm` or `none`.<br><br>Required when `factor_type` is `push`. |

| <code>identity</code> | <code>string</code> | Customer unique identity for the Entity owner of the Factor. This identifier should be immutable, not PII, length between 8 and 64 characters, and generated by your external system, such as your user's UUID, GUID, or SID. It can only contain dash (-) separated alphanumeric characters. |
| <code>friendlyName</code> | <code>string</code> | The friendly name of this Factor. This can be any string up to 64 characters, meant for humans to distinguish between Factors.<br>For `factor_type` `push`, this could be a device name.<br>For `factor_type` `totp`, this value is used as the “account name” in constructing the `binding.uri` property.<br>At the same time, we recommend avoiding providing PII. |
| <code>factorType</code> | <code>[NewFactorEnumFactorTypes](src/models/new-factor-enum-factor-types.ts)</code> | The Type of this Factor. Currently `push` and `totp` are supported. |
| <code>bindingAlg?</code> | <code>string</code> | The algorithm used when `factor_type` is `push`. Algorithm supported: `ES256` |
| <code>bindingPublicKey?</code> | <code>string</code> | The Ecdsa public key in PKIX, ASN.1 DER format encoded in Base64.<br><br>Required when `factor_type` is `push` |
| <code>configAppId?</code> | <code>string</code> | The ID that uniquely identifies your app in the Google or Apple store, such as `com.example.myapp`. It can be up to 100 characters long.<br><br>Required when `factor_type` is `push`. |
| <code>configNotificationPlatform?</code> | <code>[NewFactorEnumNotificationPlatforms](src/models/new-factor-enum-notification-platforms.ts)</code> | - |
| <code>configNotificationToken?</code> | <code>string</code> | For APN, the device token. For FCM, the registration token. It is used to send the push notifications. Must be between 32 and 255 characters long.<br><br>Required when `factor_type` is `push`. |
| <code>configSdkVersion?</code> | <code>string</code> | The Verify Push SDK version used to configure the factor<br><br>Required when `factor_type` is `push` |
| <code>bindingSecret?</code> | <code>string</code> | The shared secret for TOTP factors encoded in Base32. This can be provided when creating the Factor, otherwise it will be generated.<br><br>Used when `factor_type` is `totp` |
| <code>configTimeStep?</code> | <code>number</code> | Defines how often, in seconds, are TOTP codes generated. i.e, a new TOTP code is generated every time_step seconds. Must be between 20 and 60 seconds, inclusive. The default value is defined at the service level in the property `totp.time_step`. Defaults to 30 seconds if not configured.<br><br>Used when `factor_type` is `totp` |
| <code>configSkew?</code> | <code>number</code> | The number of time-steps, past and future, that are valid for validation of TOTP codes. Must be between 0 and 2, inclusive. The default value is defined at the service level in the property `totp.skew`. If not configured defaults to 1.<br><br>Used when `factor_type` is `totp` |
| <code>configCodeLength?</code> | <code>number</code> | Number of digits for generated TOTP codes. Must be between 3 and 8, inclusive. The default value is defined at the service level in the property `totp.code_length`. If not configured defaults to 6.<br><br>Used when `factor_type` is `totp` |
| <code>configAlg?</code> | <code>[NewFactorEnumTotpAlgorithms](src/models/new-factor-enum-totp-algorithms.ts)</code> | - |
| <code>metadata?</code> | <code>Record&lt;string, unknown&gt;</code> | Custom metadata associated with the factor. This is added by the Device/SDK directly to allow for the inclusion of device information. It must be a stringified JSON with only strings values eg. `{"os": "Android"}`. Can be up to 1024 characters in length. |

| <code>codeLength?</code> | <code>number</code> | The length of the verification code to generate. Must be an integer value between 4 and 10, inclusive. |
| <code>lookupEnabled?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether to perform a lookup with each verification started and return info about the phone number. |
| <code>skipSmsToLandlines?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether to skip sending SMS verifications to landlines. Requires `lookup_enabled`. |
| <code>dtmfInputRequired?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether to ask the user to press a number before delivering the verify code in a phone call. |
| <code>ttsName?</code> | <code>string</code> | The name of an alternative text-to-speech service to use in phone calls. Applies only to TTS languages. |
| <code>psd2Enabled?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether to pass PSD2 transaction parameters when starting a verification. |
| <code>doNotShareWarningEnabled?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether to add a security warning at the end of an SMS verification body. Disabled by default and applies only to SMS. Example SMS body: `Your AppName verification code is: 1234. Don’t share this code with anyone; our employees will never ask for the code` |
| <code>customCodeEnabled?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether to allow sending verifications with a custom code instead of a randomly generated one. |
| <code>pushIncludeDate?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Optional configuration for the Push factors. If true, include the date in the Challenge's response. Otherwise, the date is omitted from the response. See [Challenge](https://www.twilio.com/docs/verify/api/challenge) resource’s details parameter for more info. Default: false. **Deprecated** do not use this parameter. This timestamp value is the same one as the one found in `date_created`, please use that one instead. |
| <code>pushApnCredentialSid?</code> | <code>string</code> | Optional configuration for the Push factors. Set the APN Credential for this service. This will allow to send push notifications to iOS devices. See [Credential Resource](https://www.twilio.com/docs/notify/api/credential-resource) |
| <code>pushFcmCredentialSid?</code> | <code>string</code> | Optional configuration for the Push factors. Set the FCM Credential for this service. This will allow to send push notifications to Android devices. See [Credential Resource](https://www.twilio.com/docs/notify/api/credential-resource) |
| <code>totpIssuer?</code> | <code>string</code> | Optional configuration for the TOTP factors. Set TOTP Issuer for this service. This will allow to configure the issuer of the TOTP URI. Defaults to the service friendly name if not provided. |
| <code>totpTimeStep?</code> | <code>number</code> | Optional configuration for the TOTP factors. Defines how often, in seconds, are TOTP codes generated. i.e, a new TOTP code is generated every time_step seconds. Must be between 20 and 60 seconds, inclusive. Defaults to 30 seconds |
| <code>totpCodeLength?</code> | <code>number</code> | Optional configuration for the TOTP factors. Number of digits for generated TOTP codes. Must be between 3 and 8, inclusive. Defaults to 6 |
| <code>totpSkew?</code> | <code>number</code> | Optional configuration for the TOTP factors. The number of time-steps, past and future, that are valid for validation of TOTP codes. Must be between 0 and 2, inclusive. Defaults to 1 |
| <code>defaultTemplateSid?</code> | <code>string</code> | The default message [template](https://www.twilio.com/docs/verify/api/templates). Will be used for all SMS verifications unless explicitly overriden. SMS channel only. |
| <code>whatsappMsgServiceSid?</code> | <code>string</code> | The SID of the Messaging Service containing WhatsApp Sender(s) that Verify will use to send WhatsApp messages to your users. |
| <code>whatsappFrom?</code> | <code>string</code> | The number to use as the WhatsApp Sender that Verify will use to send WhatsApp messages to your users.This WhatsApp Sender must be associated with a Messaging Service SID. |
| <code>passkeysRelyingPartyId?</code> | <code>string</code> | The Relying Party ID for Passkeys. This is the domain of your application, e.g. `example.com`. It is used to identify your application when creating Passkeys. |
| <code>passkeysRelyingPartyName?</code> | <code>string</code> | The Relying Party Name for Passkeys. This is the name of your application, e.g. `Example App`. It is used to identify your application when creating Passkeys. |
| <code>passkeysRelyingPartyOrigins?</code> | <code>string</code> | The Relying Party Origins for Passkeys. This is the origin of your application, e.g. `login.example.com,www.example.com`. It is used to identify your application when creating Passkeys, it can have multiple origins split by `,`. |
| <code>passkeysAuthenticatorAttachment?</code> | <code>string</code> | The Authenticator Attachment for Passkeys. This is the type of authenticator that will be used to create Passkeys. It can be empty or it can have the values `platform`, `cross-platform` or `any`. |
| <code>passkeysDiscoverableCredentials?</code> | <code>string</code> | Indicates whether credentials must be discoverable by the authenticator. It can be empty or it can have the values `required`, `preferred` or `discouraged`. |
| <code>passkeysUserVerification?</code> | <code>string</code> | The User Verification for Passkeys. This is the type of user verification that will be used to create Passkeys. It can be empty or it can have the values `required`, `preferred` or `discouraged`. |
| <code>verifyEventSubscriptionEnabled?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether to allow verifications from the service to reach the stream-events sinks if configured |

| <code>lastName?</code> | <code>string</code> | User’s last name. This query parameter is only used (optionally) for identity_match package requests. |
| <code>addressLine1?</code> | <code>string</code> | User’s first address line. This query parameter is only used (optionally) for identity_match package requests. |
| <code>addressLine2?</code> | <code>string</code> | User’s second address line. This query parameter is only used (optionally) for identity_match package requests. |
| <code>city?</code> | <code>string</code> | User’s city. This query parameter is only used (optionally) for identity_match package requests. |
| <code>state?</code> | <code>string</code> | User’s country subdivision, such as state, province, or locality. This query parameter is only used (optionally) for identity_match package requests. |
| <code>postalCode?</code> | <code>string</code> | User’s postal zip code. This query parameter is only used (optionally) for identity_match package requests. |
| <code>addressCountryCode?</code> | <code>string</code> | User’s country, up to two characters. This query parameter is only used (optionally) for identity_match package requests. |
| <code>nationalId?</code> | <code>string</code> | User’s national ID, such as SSN or Passport ID. This query parameter is only used (optionally) for identity_match package requests. |
| <code>dateOfBirth?</code> | <code>string</code> | User’s date of birth, in YYYYMMDD format. This query parameter is only used (optionally) for identity_match package requests. |
| <code>lastVerifiedDate?</code> | <code>string</code> | The date you obtained consent to call or text the end-user of the phone number or a date on which you are reasonably certain that the end-user could still be reached at that number. This query parameter is only used (optionally) for reassigned_number package requests. |
| <code>verificationSid?</code> | <code>string</code> | The unique identifier associated with a verification process through verify API. This query parameter is only used (optionally) for pre_fill package requests. |
| <code>partnerSubId?</code> | <code>string</code> | The optional partnerSubId parameter to provide context for your sub-accounts, tenantIDs, sender IDs or other segmentation, enhancing the accuracy of the risk analysis. |

| Name | Type | Description |

| <code>contactPhoneNumber</code> | <code>string</code> | The contact phone number of the person authorized to sign the Authorization Document. |
| <code>addressSid</code> | <code>string</code> | Optional. A 34 character string that uniquely identifies the Address resource that represents the address of the owner of this phone number. |
| <code>email</code> | <code>string</code> | Optional. Email of the owner of this phone number that is being hosted. |
| <code>accountSid?</code> | <code>string</code> | This defaults to the AccountSid of the authorization the user is using. This can be provided to specify a subaccount to add the HostedNumberOrder to. |

| <code>ccEmails?</code> | <code>string[]</code> | Optional. A list of emails that the LOA document for this HostedNumberOrder will be carbon copied to. |
| <code>smsUrl?</code> | <code>string</code> | The URL that Twilio should request when somebody sends an SMS to the phone number. This will be copied onto the IncomingPhoneNumber resource. |
| <code>smsMethod?</code> | <code>[AmdStatusCallbackMethod](src/models/amd-status-callback-method.ts)</code> | The HTTP method that should be used to request the SmsUrl. Must be either `GET` or `POST`.  This will be copied onto the IncomingPhoneNumber resource. |
| <code>smsFallbackUrl?</code> | <code>string</code> | A URL that Twilio will request if an error occurs requesting or executing the TwiML defined by SmsUrl. This will be copied onto the IncomingPhoneNumber resource. |
| <code>smsCapability?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Used to specify that the SMS capability will be hosted on Twilio's platform. |
| <code>smsFallbackMethod?</code> | <code>[AmdStatusCallbackMethod](src/models/amd-status-callback-method.ts)</code> | The HTTP method that should be used to request the SmsFallbackUrl. Must be either `GET` or `POST`. This will be copied onto the IncomingPhoneNumber resource. |
| <code>statusCallbackUrl?</code> | <code>string</code> | Optional. The Status Callback URL attached to the IncomingPhoneNumber resource. |
| <code>statusCallbackMethod?</code> | <code>[AmdStatusCallbackMethod](src/models/amd-status-callback-method.ts)</code> | Optional. The Status Callback Method attached to the IncomingPhoneNumber resource. |
| <code>smsApplicationSid?</code> | <code>string</code> | Optional. The 34 character sid of the application Twilio should use to handle SMS messages sent to this number. If a `SmsApplicationSid` is present, Twilio will ignore all of the SMS urls above and use those set on the application. |
| <code>contactTitle?</code> | <code>string</code> | The title of the person authorized to sign the Authorization Document for this phone number. |

| Name | Type | Description |

| <code>smsCapability</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Used to specify that the SMS capability will be hosted on Twilio's platform. |
| <code>accountSid?</code> | <code>string</code> | This defaults to the AccountSid of the authorization the user is using. This can be provided to specify a subaccount to add the HostedNumberOrder to. |
| <code>friendlyName?</code> | <code>string</code> | A 64 character string that is a human readable text that describes this resource. |
| <code>uniqueName?</code> | <code>string</code> | Optional. Provides a unique and addressable name to be assigned to this HostedNumberOrder, assigned by the developer, to be optionally used in addition to SID. |
| <code>ccEmails?</code> | <code>string[]</code> | Optional. A list of emails that the LOA document for this HostedNumberOrder will be carbon copied to. |
| <code>smsUrl?</code> | <code>string</code> | The URL that Twilio should request when somebody sends an SMS to the phone number. This will be copied onto the IncomingPhoneNumber resource. |
| <code>smsMethod?</code> | <code>[AmdStatusCallbackMethod](src/models/amd-status-callback-method.ts)</code> | The HTTP method that should be used to request the SmsUrl. Must be either `GET` or `POST`.  This will be copied onto the IncomingPhoneNumber resource. |
| <code>smsFallbackUrl?</code> | <code>string</code> | A URL that Twilio will request if an error occurs requesting or executing the TwiML defined by SmsUrl. This will be copied onto the IncomingPhoneNumber resource. |
| <code>smsFallbackMethod?</code> | <code>[AmdStatusCallbackMethod](src/models/amd-status-callback-method.ts)</code> | The HTTP method that should be used to request the SmsFallbackUrl. Must be either `GET` or `POST`. This will be copied onto the IncomingPhoneNumber resource. |
| <code>statusCallbackUrl?</code> | <code>string</code> | Optional. The Status Callback URL attached to the IncomingPhoneNumber resource. |
| <code>statusCallbackMethod?</code> | <code>[AmdStatusCallbackMethod](src/models/amd-status-callback-method.ts)</code> | Optional. The Status Callback Method attached to the IncomingPhoneNumber resource. |
| <code>smsApplicationSid?</code> | <code>string</code> | Optional. The 34 character sid of the application Twilio should use to handle SMS messages sent to this number. If a `SmsApplicationSid` is present, Twilio will ignore all of the SMS urls above and use those set on the application. |
| <code>addressSid?</code> | <code>string</code> | Optional. A 34 character string that uniquely identifies the Address resource that represents the address of the owner of this phone number. |
| <code>email?</code> | <code>string</code> | Optional. Email of the owner of this phone number that is being hosted. |
| <code>verificationType?</code> | <code>[DependentOrderEnumVerificationType](src/models/dependent-order-enum-verification-type.ts)</code> | - |
| <code>verificationDocumentSid?</code> | <code>string</code> | Optional. The unique sid identifier of the Identity Document that represents the document for verifying ownership of the number to be hosted. Required when VerificationType is phone-bill. |

<dl>
<dd>

### Description

<dl>
<dd>

Recording compositions

</dd>
</dl>

### Usage

<dl>
<dd>

```ts
try {
  const response = await client.videoV1CompositionApi.createComposition({ roomSid });
  // TODO: Handle 'response' of type VideoV1Composition
} catch (err) {
  // TODO: Handle 'err' of type ResponseError
}
```

</dd>
</dl>

### Parameters

<dl>
<dd>

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code>roomSid</code> | <code>string</code> | The SID of the Group Room with the media tracks to be used as composition sources. |
| <code>videoLayout?</code> | <code>Record&lt;string, unknown&gt;</code> | An object that describes the video layout of the composition in terms of regions. See [Specifying Video Layouts](https://www.twilio.com/docs/video/api/compositions-resource#specifying-video-layouts) for more info. Please, be aware that either video_layout or audio_sources have to be provided to get a valid creation request |
| <code>audioSources?</code> | <code>string[]</code> | An array of track names from the same group room to merge into the new composition. Can include zero or more track names. The new composition includes all audio sources specified in `audio_sources` except for those specified in `audio_sources_excluded`. The track names in this parameter can include an asterisk as a wild card character, which will match zero or more characters in a track name. For example, `student*` includes `student` as well as `studentTeam`. Please, be aware that either video_layout or audio_sources have to be provided to get a valid creation request |
| <code>audioSourcesExcluded?</code> | <code>string[]</code> | An array of track names to exclude. The new composition includes all audio sources specified in `audio_sources` except for those specified in `audio_sources_excluded`. The track names in this parameter can include an asterisk as a wild card character, which will match zero or more characters in a track name. For example, `student*` excludes `student` as well as `studentTeam`. This parameter can also be empty. |
| <code>resolution?</code> | <code>string</code> | A string that describes the columns (width) and rows (height) of the generated composed video in pixels. Defaults to `640x480`. <br>The string's format is `{width}x{height}` where: <br><br>* 16 <= `{width}` <= 1280<br>* 16 <= `{height}` <= 1280<br>* `{width}` * `{height}` <= 921,600<br><br>Typical values are: <br><br>* HD = `1280x720`<br>* PAL = `1024x576`<br>* VGA = `640x480`<br>* CIF = `320x240`<br><br>Note that the `resolution` imposes an aspect ratio to the resulting composition. When the original video tracks are constrained by the aspect ratio, they are scaled to fit. See [Specifying Video Layouts](https://www.twilio.com/docs/video/api/compositions-resource#specifying-video-layouts) for more info. |
| <code>format?</code> | <code>[CompositionEnumFormat](src/models/composition-enum-format.ts)</code> | The container format of the composition's media files as specified in the POST request that created the Composition resource. See [POST Parameters](https://www.twilio.com/docs/video/api/compositions-resource#http-post-parameters) for more information. |
| <code>statusCallback?</code> | <code>string</code> | The URL we should call using the `status_callback_method` to send status information to your application on every composition event. If not provided, status callback events will not be dispatched. |
| <code>statusCallbackMethod?</code> | <code>[AmdStatusCallbackMethod](src/models/amd-status-callback-method.ts)</code> | The HTTP method we should use to call `status_callback`. Can be: `POST` or `GET` and the default is `POST`. |
| <code>trim?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether to clip the intervals where there is no active media in the composition. The default is `true`. Compositions with `trim` enabled are shorter when the Room is created and no Participant joins for a while as well as if all the Participants leave the room and join later, because those gaps will be removed. See [Specifying Video Layouts](https://www.twilio.com/docs/video/api/compositions-resource#specifying-video-layouts) for more info. |

</dd>
</dl>

<dl>
<dd>

<dl>

Recording composition hooks

<dl>
<dd>

```ts
try {
  const response = await client.videoV1CompositionHookApi.createCompositionHook({ friendlyName });
  // TODO: Handle 'response' of type VideoV1CompositionHook

  // TODO: Handle 'err' of type ResponseError
}
```

</dd>
</dl>

### Parameters

<dl>
<dd>

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code>friendlyName</code> | <code>string</code> | A descriptive string that you create to describe the resource. It can be up to  100 characters long and it must be unique within the account. |
| <code>enabled?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether the composition hook is active. When `true`, the composition hook will be triggered for every completed Group Room in the account. When `false`, the composition hook will never be triggered. |
| <code>videoLayout?</code> | <code>Record&lt;string, unknown&gt;</code> | An object that describes the video layout of the composition hook in terms of regions. See [Specifying Video Layouts](https://www.twilio.com/docs/video/api/compositions-resource#specifying-video-layouts) for more info. |
| <code>audioSources?</code> | <code>string[]</code> | An array of track names from the same group room to merge into the compositions created by the composition hook. Can include zero or more track names. A composition triggered by the composition hook includes all audio sources specified in `audio_sources` except those specified in `audio_sources_excluded`. The track names in this parameter can include an asterisk as a wild card character, which matches zero or more characters in a track name. For example, `student*` includes tracks named `student` as well as `studentTeam`. |
| <code>audioSourcesExcluded?</code> | <code>string[]</code> | An array of track names to exclude. A composition triggered by the composition hook includes all audio sources specified in `audio_sources` except for those specified in `audio_sources_excluded`. The track names in this parameter can include an asterisk as a wild card character, which matches zero or more characters in a track name. For example, `student*` excludes `student` as well as `studentTeam`. This parameter can also be empty. |
| <code>resolution?</code> | <code>string</code> | A string that describes the columns (width) and rows (height) of the generated composed video in pixels. Defaults to `640x480`. <br>The string's format is `{width}x{height}` where: <br><br>* 16 <= `{width}` <= 1280<br>* 16 <= `{height}` <= 1280<br>* `{width}` * `{height}` <= 921,600<br><br>Typical values are: <br><br>* HD = `1280x720`<br>* PAL = `1024x576`<br>* VGA = `640x480`<br>* CIF = `320x240`<br><br>Note that the `resolution` imposes an aspect ratio to the resulting composition. When the original video tracks are constrained by the aspect ratio, they are scaled to fit. See [Specifying Video Layouts](https://www.twilio.com/docs/video/api/compositions-resource#specifying-video-layouts) for more info. |
| <code>format?</code> | <code>[CompositionHookEnumFormat](src/models/composition-hook-enum-format.ts)</code> | The container format of the media files used by the compositions created by the composition hook. If `mp4` or `webm`, `audio_sources` must have one or more tracks and/or a `video_layout` element must contain a valid `video_sources` list, otherwise an error occurs. |
| <code>statusCallback?</code> | <code>string</code> | The URL we should call using the `status_callback_method` to send status information to your application on every composition event. If not provided, status callback events will not be dispatched. |
| <code>statusCallbackMethod?</code> | <code>[AmdStatusCallbackMethod](src/models/amd-status-callback-method.ts)</code> | The HTTP method we should use to call `status_callback`. Can be: `POST` or `GET` and the default is `POST`. |
| <code>trim?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether to clip the intervals where there is no active media in the Compositions triggered by the composition hook. The default is `true`. Compositions with `trim` enabled are shorter when the Room is created and no Participant joins for a while as well as if all the Participants leave the room and join later, because those gaps will be removed. See [Specifying Video Layouts](https://www.twilio.com/docs/video/api/compositions-resource#specifying-video-layouts) for more info. |

</dd>
</dl>

| <code>recordParticipantsOnConnect?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether to start recording when Participants connect. |
| <code>transcribeParticipantsOnConnect?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether to start transcriptions when Participants connect. If TranscriptionsConfiguration is not provided, default settings will be used. |

| <code>recordingRules?</code> | <code>Record&lt;string, unknown&gt;</code> | A collection of Recording Rules that describe how to include or exclude matching tracks for recording |
| <code>transcriptionsConfiguration?</code> | <code>Record&lt;string, unknown&gt;</code> | A collection of properties that describe transcription behaviour. If TranscribeParticipantsOnConnect is set to true and TranscriptionsConfiguration is not provided, default settings will be used. |
| <code>audioOnly?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | When set to true, indicates that the participants in the room will only publish audio. No video tracks will be allowed. |
| <code>maxParticipantDuration?</code> | <code>number</code> | The maximum number of seconds a Participant can be connected to the room. The maximum possible value is 86400 seconds (24 hours). The default is 14400 seconds (4 hours). |
| <code>emptyRoomTimeout?</code> | <code>number</code> | Configures how long (in minutes) a room will remain active after last participant leaves. Valid values range from 1 to 60 minutes (no fractions). |
| <code>unusedRoomTimeout?</code> | <code>number</code> | Configures how long (in minutes) a room will remain active if no one joins. Valid values range from 1 to 60 minutes (no fractions). |

<dl>
<dd>

### Description

<dl>
<dd>

Retrieve a list of conversations in your account's default service

</dd>
</dl>

### Usage

<dl>
<dd>

```ts
try {
  const response = await client.conversationsV1ConversationApi.listConversation();
  // TODO: Handle 'response' of type ListConversationResponse
} catch (err) {

}
```

</dd>

### Parameters

<dl>
<dd>

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code>startDate?</code> | <code>string</code> | Specifies the beginning of the date range for filtering Conversations based on their creation date. Conversations that were created on or after this date will be included in the results. The date must be in ISO8601 format, specifically starting at the beginning of the specified date (YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00Z), for precise filtering. This parameter can be combined with other filters. If this filter is used, the returned list is sorted by latest conversation creation date in descending order. |
| <code>endDate?</code> | <code>string</code> | Defines the end of the date range for filtering conversations by their creation date. Only conversations that were created on or before this date will appear in the results.  The date must be in ISO8601 format, specifically capturing up to the end of the specified date (YYYY-MM-DDT23:59:59Z), to ensure that conversations from the entire end day are included. This parameter can be combined with other filters. If this filter is used, the returned list is sorted by latest conversation creation date in descending order. |
| <code>state?</code> | <code>[ConversationEnumState](src/models/conversation-enum-state.ts)</code> | State for sorting and filtering list of Conversations. Can be `active`, `inactive` or `closed` |
| <code>pageSize?</code> | <code>number</code> | How many resources to return in each list page. The default is 50, and the maximum is 100. |
| <code>page?</code> | <code>number</code> | The page index. This value is simply for client state. |
| <code>pageToken?</code> | <code>string</code> | The page token. This is provided by the API. |

</dd>

The default value is 24 hours (86,400 seconds). On timeout, the `task.canceled` event will fire with description `Task TTL Exceeded`. |

Value can be 0 to 2^31^ (2,147,483,647). |
| <code>taskChannel?</code> | <code>string</code> | When MultiTasking is enabled, specify the TaskChannel by passing either its `unique_name` or `sid`. Default value is `default`. |
| <code>workflowSid?</code> | <code>string</code> | The SID of the Workflow that you would like to handle routing for the new Task. If there is only one Workflow defined for the Workspace that you are posting the new task to, this parameter is optional. |
| <code>attributes?</code> | <code>string</code> | A JSON string with the attributes of the new task. This value is passed to the Workflow's `assignment_callback_url` when the Task is assigned to a Worker. For example: `{ "task_type": "call", "twilio_call_sid": "CAxxx", "customer_ticket_number": "12345" }`. |
| <code>virtualStartTime?</code> | <code>Date</code> (date-time) | The virtual start time to assign the new task and override the default. When supplied, the new task will have this virtual start time. When not supplied, the new task will have the virtual start time equal to `date_created`. Value can't be in the future or before the year of 1900. |
| <code>routingTarget?</code> | <code>string</code> | A SID of a Worker, Queue, or Workflow to route a Task to |
| <code>ignoreCapacity?</code> | <code>string</code> | A boolean that indicates if the Task should respect a Worker's capacity and availability during assignment. This field can only be used when the `RoutingTarget` field is set to a Worker SID. By setting `IgnoreCapacity` to a value of `true`, `1`, or `yes`, the Task will be routed to the Worker without respecting their capacity and availability. Any other value will enforce the Worker's capacity and availability. The default value of `IgnoreCapacity` is `true` when the `RoutingTarget` is set to a Worker SID. |
| <code>taskQueueSid?</code> | <code>string</code> | The SID of the TaskQueue in which the Task belongs |

<dl>

| <code>workflowSid</code> | <code>string</code> | Returns the list of Tasks that are being controlled by the Workflow with the specified Sid value. |
| <code>endDate?</code> | <code>Date</code> (date-time) | Only include usage that occurred on or before this date, specified in GMT as an [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) date-time. |
| <code>minutes?</code> | <code>number</code> | Only calculate statistics since this many minutes in the past. The default 15 minutes. This is helpful for displaying statistics for the last 15 minutes, 240 minutes (4 hours), and 480 minutes (8 hours) to see trends. |
| <code>startDate?</code> | <code>Date</code> (date-time) | Only calculate statistics from this date and time and later, specified in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format. |
| <code>taskChannel?</code> | <code>string</code> | Only calculate cumulative statistics on this TaskChannel. Can be the TaskChannel's SID or its `unique_name`, such as `voice`, `sms`, or `default`. |
| <code>splitByWaitTime?</code> | <code>string</code> | A comma separated list of values that describes the thresholds, in seconds, to calculate statistics on. For each threshold specified, the number of Tasks canceled and reservations accepted above and below the specified thresholds in seconds are computed. For example, `5,30` would show splits of Tasks that were canceled or accepted before and after 5 seconds and before and after 30 seconds. This can be used to show short abandoned Tasks or Tasks that failed to meet an SLA. TaskRouter will calculate statistics on up to 10,000 Tasks for any given threshold. |

### Parameters

<dl>

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <code>friendlyName</code> | <code>string</code> | A descriptive string that you create to describe the Workspace resource. It can be up to 64 characters long. For example: `Customer Support` or `2014 Election Campaign`. |
| <code>eventCallbackUrl?</code> | <code>string</code> | The URL we should call when an event occurs. If provided, the Workspace will publish events to this URL, for example, to collect data for reporting. See [Workspace Events](https://www.twilio.com/docs/taskrouter/api/event) for more information. This parameter supports Twilio's [Webhooks (HTTP callbacks) Connection Overrides](https://www.twilio.com/docs/usage/webhooks/webhooks-connection-overrides). |
| <code>eventsFilter?</code> | <code>string</code> | The list of Workspace events for which to call event_callback_url. For example, if `EventsFilter=task.created, task.canceled, worker.activity.update`, then TaskRouter will call event_callback_url only when a task is created, canceled, or a Worker activity is updated. |
| <code>multiTaskEnabled?</code> | <code>boolean</code> | Whether to enable multi-tasking. Can be: `true` to enable multi-tasking, or `false` to disable it. However, all workspaces should be created as multi-tasking. The default is `true`. Multi-tasking allows Workers to handle multiple Tasks simultaneously. When enabled (`true`), each Worker can receive parallel reservations up to the per-channel maximums defined in the Workers section. In single-tasking mode (legacy mode), each Worker will only receive a new reservation when the previous task is completed. Learn more at [Multitasking](https://www.twilio.com/docs/taskrouter/multitasking). |
| <code>template?</code> | <code>string</code> | An available template name. Can be: `NONE` or `FIFO` and the default is `NONE`. Pre-configures the Workspace with the Workflow and Activities specified in the template. `NONE` will create a Workspace with only a set of default activities. `FIFO` will configure TaskRouter with a set of default activities and a single TaskQueue for first-in, first-out distribution, which can be useful when you are getting started with TaskRouter. |
| <code>prioritizeQueueOrder?</code> | <code>[WorkspaceEnumQueueOrder](src/models/workspace-enum-queue-order.ts)</code> | The type of TaskQueue to prioritize when Workers are receiving Tasks from both types of TaskQueues. Can be: `LIFO` or `FIFO` and the default is `FIFO`. For more information, see [Queue Ordering](https://www.twilio.com/docs/taskrouter/queue-ordering-last-first-out-lifo). |

</dd>

| <code>minutes?</code> | <code>number</code> | Only calculate statistics since this many minutes in the past. The default 15 minutes. This is helpful for displaying statistics for the last 15 minutes, 240 minutes (4 hours), and 480 minutes (8 hours) to see trends. |
| <code>startDate?</code> | <code>Date</code> (date-time) | Only calculate statistics from this date and time and later, specified in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format. |
| <code>endDate?</code> | <code>Date</code> (date-time) | Only calculate statistics from this date and time and earlier, specified in GMT as an [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) date-time. |
| <code>taskChannel?</code> | <code>string</code> | Only calculate statistics on this TaskChannel. Can be the TaskChannel's SID or its `unique_name`, such as `voice`, `sms`, or `default`. |
| <code>splitByWaitTime?</code> | <code>string</code> | A comma separated list of values that describes the thresholds, in seconds, to calculate statistics on. For each threshold specified, the number of Tasks canceled and reservations accepted above and below the specified thresholds in seconds are computed. For example, `5,30` would show splits of Tasks that were canceled or accepted before and after 5 seconds and before and after 30 seconds. This can be used to show short abandoned Tasks or Tasks that failed to meet an SLA. |

</dd>
</dl>

</dd>

```ts
}
```
